newsitem.title: UK: Axa Belgian options still open - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Axa Belgian options still open - analysts.

text.p: French insurer Axa-UAP is expected to sell one of its two Belgian subsidiaries, but London based analysts said on Friday which one will go and when has yet to be decided.
"Axa already had a decent business in Belgium before the UAP acquisition, so it was always on the cards to sell one or the other -- it could go either way," said one insurance analyst.
French newspaper Le Monde earlier reported that Axa will announce on May 28 the sale of Royale Belge. The report was denied by AXA-Belgium chief executive Patrick de Courcel.

"I know there are lots of rumours in the market and the press at the moment, that we (AXA Belgium) or Royale Belge will be sold, but it's all crazy. Everything is pure speculation. There's nothing behind it," he told Reuters earlier.
Axa bought UAP last November and with it a controlling stake in Royale Belge, the second biggest Belgian insurer. Axa already owned Axa-Belgium, the fifth largest insurer in the country.
There is no pressure on Axa to sell either unit from a regulatory stance, a spokesman for Axa in Paris told Reuters.

However, in the longer term, analysts believe that the group will sell one of the companies rather than opt for a merger, which would take up a lot of management energy at a time when Axa-UAP has more pressing tasks, such as rationalising its French operations.

They said a case for selling either subsidiary could be made. Keeping Royale Belge would give Axa a larger share of the Belgian market, but integrating it into the group would be harder than keeping the majority owned Axa-Belgium.
The latter, being a wholly owned unit, would make a more attractive proposition to a prospective buyer, analysts said.
Switzerland's Winterthur Insurance Co and ING Groep NV, both named as potential buyers in press reports, said they had no comment to make.
Apart from ING and Winterthur, analysts said Allianz and Generali were in the frame as possible predators, with Royal & Sun Alliance Plc very much an outsider.
According to 1995 figures, Axa-Belgium and Royale Belge had 15 percent of the Belgian life insurance market and around 20 percent of the non-life market.
Shares in Royale Belge pushed ahead to a new high for the year of 10,250 Belgian francs, before slipping back to 9,920 in late afternoon trade.
Analysts said the possibility of a sale was largely reflected in the price.
